---
title: "Model passport"
description: "A one-page model passport: the empty template and a completed teaching example for the fracture-alert baseline from Lab W3."
---















A model passport is one page that lets a person outside the group judge what a model was built for, on which data
it was tested and where its evidence ends. It travels with the model: every new version gets an updated passport.
Every entry is either a fact with its source, a number with its denominator, or an *open* point together with the
information that would close it.

## Template

Copy the table into your project and fill in every row. Leave nothing blank: write *open* and what is missing.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| **Name and version** | |
| **Intended purpose** (one sentence: who uses it, for whom, to do what) | |
| **Decision supported** and what happens without the model | |
| **Target population and setting** | |
| **Data source and status** (*synthetic*, *published*, released for teaching) | |
| **Unit of analysis and independent denominator** | |
| **Time zero and prediction horizon** | |
| **Outcome and reference standard** | |
| **Predictors** (available at time zero?) | |
| **Baseline** for comparison | |
| **Model** and tuning (on which data?) | |
| **Validation design** (split, test identifiers, external data?) | |
| **Performance with uncertainty** (discrimination, calibration, errors at the threshold as *x*/*n*) | |
| **Errors by subgroup** (with denominators) | |
| **Counter-check** (what was changed, what was predicted, what happened) | |
| **Not tested** (populations, devices, time periods) | |
| **Limits of the claim** | |
| **Reproducibility** (script, start command, seed, R version) | |
| **Open points**, the information that would close each, and the responsible role | |

## Worked teaching example: fracture-alert baseline

All numbers come from the *synthetic* data of [Lab W3](lab-w3-diagnostic-accuracy.qmd) and are computed when this
page is rendered.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| **Name and version** | Fracture-alert baseline, teaching version 1.0 (logistic regression, four predictors). |
| **Intended purpose** | For adults with a suspected wrist fracture in the emergency department, prompt a second review of the radiograph before discharge. *Teaching purpose only; not authorised for use in care.* |
| **Decision supported** | Second review of the radiograph yes/no. Without the model: usual single reading and routine follow-up. |
| **Target population and setting** | Adults (18–95 years) presenting with wrist pain after a fall; one fictitious emergency department. |
| **Data source and status** | *Synthetic* cohort of 2,000 admissions generated in `r/w3-diagnostic-accuracy.R` with seed 20260309. |
| **Unit of analysis and independent denominator** | One admission per person; test set 600 admissions with 84 fractures. |
| **Time zero and prediction horizon** | Time zero: clinical examination before imaging. Outcome: fracture according to the reference standard. |
| **Outcome and reference standard** | Fracture yes/no; reference standard assumed complete for everyone (*assumption*; in practice follow-up imaging). |
| **Predictors** | Age, fall on outstretched hand, snuffbox tenderness, swelling; all available at time zero. |
| **Baseline** | Null model with the training prevalence (Brier score 0.121). |
| **Model** and tuning | Logistic regression, no tuning. Alternative for comparison: elastic net with interactions, penalty tuned by five-fold cross-validation inside the 1400 training admissions. |
| **Validation design** | One fixed random split (1400 training, 600 test); test identifiers stored with the data; zero shared identifiers. Internal validation only. |
| **Performance with uncertainty** | AUC 0.858; Brier score 0.091; calibration slope 0.86 (overestimates risk in the highest risk group). At a threshold of 20%: detects 60/84 = 71.4% (60.5% to 80.8%) of fractures; false alerts in 103/516 = 20.0% (16.6% to 23.7%) of people without fracture. |
| **Errors by subgroup** | Detected fractures, age 18–74: 35/46 = 76.1% (61.2% to 87.4%); age 75 and older: 25/38 = 65.8% (48.6% to 80.4%). False alerts, age 75 and older: 43/131 = 32.8% (24.9% to 41.6%). |
| **Counter-check** | The elastic net, predicted to rank clearly better, improved the AUC by only 0.024 on the same test admissions. |
| **Not tested** | Other hospitals, other imaging devices, children, time periods after development, effect on patient outcomes. |
| **Limits of the claim** | Internal, synthetic validation of discrimination and calibration. No statement about benefit for patients or workload. |
| **Reproducibility** | `Rscript r/w3-diagnostic-accuracy.R` in a fresh session; target values checked with `stopifnot()`; R 4.6.1. |
| **Open points** | (1) Performance in the target hospital: needs a local, prospective accuracy study (research lead). (2) Lower sensitivity in older patients: needs real local data on this subgroup (clinical lead). (3) Intended purpose for care: needs regulatory classification (manufacturer's regulatory affairs; see W7). |

## How the passport is used in the course

- **W4, unit 16:** first version for your own project; the other group checks whether every number has its
  denominator.
- **W6, unit 24:** another group reproduces one number of the passport from a fresh R session.
- **W8:** the passport is one of the three documents you defend; the rubric criterion "R analysis, validation and
  uncertainty" is scored mainly from it.
